chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all together, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Dureys al-Kunasi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him).

Regarding a Christian who killed a Muslim, so when he was seized, he became a Muslim. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Kill him due to it.' It was said: 'And if he had not become a Muslim?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He would be handed over to the guardians of the killed one [if they wish, they kill him, and if they wish, they pardon him, and if they wish, they enslave him, and if there was wealth with him, it would be handed over to the guardians of the killed one], him and his wealth.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a Christian who kills a Muslim and then converts to Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of 'Qisas' (retaliation) in Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing that the killer's status as a non-Muslim does not exempt him from execution even if he converts, highlighting the priority of the victim's right over the killer's new religious status. The ruling grants the victim's heirs discretionary power to choose between execution, pardon, enslavement, or financial compensation, reflecting the flexibility of Islamic penal law. This narration is central to understanding the legal distinction between the blood money (Diya) and the right to life in cases of inter-faith homicide.
